title: QUIC flows hang when allow_hosts or ignore_hosts is enabled
answers: Why do QUIC flows stall forever after TLS handshake when ignore_hosts is enabled?
Why are QUIC connections not assigned an HttpLayer or appearing in mitmweb?
How to fix NeedsMoreData bailing out next_layer on UDP streams?
body:
Symptom: QUIC connections stall indefinitely after client handshake without assigning an HttpLayer or appearing in mitmweb when --allow-hosts or --ignore-hosts is configured.
Root cause: mitmproxy/addons/next_layer.py:_get_client_hello fell back unconditionally to dtls_parse_client_hello on UDP payloads, which raised NeedsMoreData on non-DTLS data.
Fix pattern: Guard protocol ClientHello parsers with heuristic format checks (_starts_like_quic, starts_like_dtls_record) and return None if neither matches.
Constraints: Applies to speculative ClientHello sniffing on UDP in next_layer; only raise NeedsMoreData when a recognized protocol header is partially received.
applies: mitmproxy/addons/next_layer.py UDP ClientHello detection and host filtering
says: Fast web traffic hangs indefinitely when domain ignore or allow filters are active.
Modern UDP connections freeze after the initial handshake and never appear in traffic list.
Web browser stalls forever loading sites when proxy filtering rules are turned on.
Fix stalled streaming connections when using domain allow lists with modern web protocols.
